EmailReceivedEvent
userId, receivedAtMessageId,
origin: receive | backfill (NEW required field)
(published per stored row,
audit partition included)

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
operator backfill (backfill-email-links)
deletes the email's link rows + meta,
republishes so the DEPLOYED extraction
re-classifies previews — never saves

extract + cap links, classify,
one batched LLM triage per email

span.p:
re-delivery check:
row already terminal — publish nothing;
row still pending — publish both again
(consumers idempotent)

origin = receive
AND userId is not UNROUTED_USER_ID
AND validateSaveableUrl SUCCESS

SubmitLinkCommand userId, url
published FIRST

span.p:
no queue save:
backfill replay, audit-partition mail
(no real user), or unsaveable URL
(localhost / private IP / oversized / non-http)

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
CrawlEmailLinkPreview
published SECOND, after the submit:
its consumer flips the row terminal, so
preview-first plus a crash between the two
publishes would let the retry's pending-gate
silently skip a submit that never happened
